rules.rounding: half up, as JavaScript Math.round in build.js
rules.ranking: competition ranking on the rounded overall, ties share the best rank, as build.js
rules.bands: applied to the rounded overall, edges as build.js BANDS
rules.intervals: 5th and 95th percentiles of the draws (inverted CDF, so every bound is an attained rank)
rules.geometric: weighted geometric mean of unscaled 0-100 scores (min score 20, no zeros)
rules.leaveOneOut: drop one category, rescale the other seven weights to sum to 100
rules.dirichlet: weights drawn from a Dirichlet with alpha equal to the published weight in points, published scores
rules.band25: each weight times an independent uniform factor in [0.75, 1.25], rescaled to sum to 100, published scores
rules.band50: each weight times an independent uniform factor in [0.5, 1.5], rescaled to sum to 100, published scores
rules.noise5: independent uniform on [-5, +5] per category score, clipped to [0, 100], published weights
rules.noise5Shared: pessimistic bound: one uniform [-5, +5] offset per country applied to all eight of its categories (a rater generous or harsh to a whole country)
rules.combined: Dirichlet weights and noise together in one draw (Handbook 7.1)
rules.calibratedCell: normal error per category score, SD 6.24 (blind re-scoring limits of agreement / 1.96 / 2 / sqrt 2), published weights
rules.calibratedShared: normal error per category score SD 5.0 plus one shared offset per country SD 2.0, published weights
rules.calibratedCombined: the calibratedShared error with Dirichlet weights in the same draw; the MAIN model for published rank ranges

meta.leadRule: a country is called first alone only if it is first in at least 95% of MAIN draws; otherwise name every country whose MAIN 90% rank range includes 1

keysModel.note: controlModel is a coded judgement, not a function of scores or weights; nothing here can test it

handbook.citation: OECD/European Commission Joint Research Centre (2008). Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators: Methodology and User Guide. Nardo M, Saisana M, Saltelli A, Tarantola S (JRC); Hoffmann A, Giovannini E (OECD). OECD Publishing, Paris. ISBN 978-92-64-04345-9.

passages.section 1.7, pp. 34-35: lists sources of uncertainty to test, including 'Using different aggregation systems, e.g. linear, geometric mean' and 'Using different plausible values for the weights'; results 'generally reported as country rankings with their related uncertainty bounds'
passages.Step 7 opens p. 117; eq. 38, p. 118: average shift in rank R_S = (1/M) sum |Rank_ref(CI_c) - Rank(CI_c)|
passages.7.1, p. 118: the analysis is conducted as a single Monte Carlo experiment, exploring all uncertainty sources simultaneously
passages.Figure 18, p. 125: original rank, median rank and 5th and 95th percentile bounds of the Monte Carlo ranks

meta.synthetic: Every interval is a simulation under the stated assumptions about weights and rater precision, not a measurement.
